stem: The three main styles of Indian temple architecture are Nagara, Dravida and __________.
solution: The three broad styles are Nagara (north), Dravida (south) and Vesara (hybrid, Deccan).

stem: The Nagara style of temple architecture is associated with __________ India.
solution: The Nagara style is the northern Indian temple style.

stem: The Dravida style of temple architecture is associated with __________ India.
solution: The Dravida style is the southern Indian temple style.

stem: The curvilinear tower over the sanctum in a Nagara temple is called the __________.
solution: In Nagara temples the tower over the sanctum is the shikhara.

stem: The pyramidal tower over the sanctum in a Dravida temple is called the __________.
solution: In Dravida temples the tower over the sanctum is the vimana.

stem: The sanctum sanctorum housing the main deity is called the __________.
solution: The garbhagriha ('womb chamber') is the sanctum housing the main deity.

stem: The monumental gateway tower of a South Indian temple complex is called the __________.
solution: The gopuram is the towering gateway of Dravida temple complexes.

stem: The ribbed, cushion-like stone disc at the top of a Nagara shikhara is the __________.
solution: The amalaka is the ribbed disc near the top of a Nagara shikhara.

stem: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, a fine Nagara temple, is at __________.
solution: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple is the finest of the Khajuraho temples.

stem: The Khajuraho temples were built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela rulers.

stem: The Sun Temple at Konark is designed in the form of a colossal __________.
solution: The Konark Sun Temple is conceived as a giant chariot of the Sun god with wheels and horses.

stem: The Konark Sun Temple was built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Konark temple was built by the Eastern Ganga ruler Narasimhadeva I.

stem: The Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur was built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Brihadeshwara temple was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I.

stem: The Shore Temple and the Rathas at Mahabalipuram were built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Mahabalipuram monuments were built by the Pallavas.

stem: The 'Pancha Rathas' at Mahabalipuram are __________ temples.
options: monolithic (each carved from a single rock)
solution: The Pancha Rathas are monolithic temples each carved from a single rock.

stem: The great relief 'Descent of the Ganga' (Arjuna's Penance) is at __________.
solution: The huge rock relief 'Descent of the Ganga' is at Mahabalipuram.

stem: The Vesara style, combining Nagara and Dravida features, developed in the __________ region.
solution: The Vesara (hybrid) style developed in the Deccan, especially Karnataka.

stem: The Hoysala temples at Belur and Halebid are known for their __________.
solution: Hoysala temples have a star-shaped (stellate) plan and extremely intricate carving.

stem: The Hoysala temples were built using __________.
solution: Hoysala temples used soft soapstone, allowing very fine carving.

stem: The pillared hall in front of the sanctum where devotees gather is the __________.
solution: The mandapa is the pillared assembly hall in front of the sanctum.

stem: The temples at Modhera and Mount Abu (Dilwara) belong to the __________ region and dynasty.
solution: The Modhera Sun Temple and Dilwara Jain temples belong to the Solanki (Maru-Gurjara) style.

stem: The Dilwara temples at Mount Abu are famous for their exquisite __________ carving.
solution: The Dilwara Jain temples are renowned for their intricate white marble carving.

stem: The Lingaraja temple, a major Nagara temple, is located at __________.
solution: The Lingaraja temple is in Bhubaneswar, Odisha (Kalinga style of Nagara).

stem: The Odisha (Kalinga) sub-style of Nagara architecture is well seen at __________.
solution: The Kalinga sub-style flourished at Bhubaneswar, Puri and Konark.

stem: The tall tower of an Odishan temple is called the __________.
solution: In Odishan (Kalinga) temples the sanctum tower is called the deul.

stem: The porch or hall in front of the deul in an Odishan temple is the __________.
solution: The jagamohana is the assembly hall (porch) in Odishan temples.

stem: The temples at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal represent early experiments by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Chalukyas at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal experimented with temple forms.

stem: Aihole is often called the '__________ of Indian temple architecture'.
solution: Aihole is called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture' for its early experiments.

stem: The erotic sculptures of Khajuraho are carved on the __________ of the temples.
solution: The famous sculptures, including erotic mithunas, are on the outer walls of Khajuraho temples.

stem: The Nagara temple usually stands on a raised platform called the __________.
solution: The Nagara temple often rests on a raised platform (jagati/adhisthana).

stem: The pot-shaped finial at the very top of a temple tower is the __________.
solution: The kalasha is the pot-shaped finial crowning the temple tower.

stem: The Dravida temple is usually enclosed within a __________.
solution: Dravida temples stand within a walled enclosure entered through gopurams.

stem: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram was built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram was built by the Pallavas.

stem: The great gopurams became especially tall and dominant under the __________ rulers.
solution: Under the Vijayanagara and Nayaka rulers the gopurams grew very tall and elaborate.

stem: The Meenakshi temple at Madurai, famous for its towering gopurams, was developed under the __________.
solution: The Meenakshi temple at Madurai was greatly developed under the Nayaka rulers.

stem: The temple, in Indian tradition, is regarded as the __________ of the deity.
solution: A temple is regarded as the residence (house) of the deity.

stem: The wheels of the Konark Sun Temple also function as __________.
solution: The carved wheels of Konark can function as sundials.

stem: The word 'Dravida' style temples are found mainly in the region of __________.
solution: Dravida temples are concentrated in Tamil Nadu and adjacent southern regions.

stem: The circumambulatory passage around the sanctum is called the __________.
solution: The pradakshina patha is the circumambulatory path around the sanctum.

stem: The temples of Khajuraho are built of __________.
solution: The Khajuraho temples are built of sandstone.

stem: The Brihadeshwara temple is famous for its very tall __________.
solution: The Brihadeshwara temple has an exceptionally tall vimana over the sanctum.

stem: The Chola bronzes, especially of Nataraja, are associated with the temples of __________.
solution: The famous Chola Nataraja bronzes come from the temples of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The Nataraja bronze depicts Shiva as the __________.
solution: Nataraja depicts Shiva as the lord of cosmic dance.

stem: The sculptural decoration of temples served to __________.
options: depict deities, myths and auspicious motifs
solution: Temple sculpture depicts deities, mythological scenes and auspicious motifs.

stem: The Elephanta cave temple, dedicated to Shiva, is near __________.
solution: The Elephanta caves are on an island near Mumbai.

stem: The famous 'Trimurti' (Sadashiva) sculpture is found at __________.
solution: The colossal three-headed Trimurti of Shiva is at the Elephanta caves.

stem: The gopuram is generally __________ the vimana in later Dravida temples.
solution: In later Dravida temples, the gateway gopurams became taller than the central vimana.

stem: The main difference between Nagara and Dravida temples lies in the shape of their __________.
solution: The chief difference is the tower form (curvilinear shikhara vs pyramidal vimana) and overall layout.

stem: The overall purpose of temple architecture was to create a __________.
options: sacred space linking the human and divine
solution: Temple architecture created a sacred space connecting the human and the divine.

stem: The rich variety of temple styles across India reflects its __________.
options: regional diversity and long architectural tradition
solution: The many temple styles reflect India's regional diversity and long architectural heritage.
